task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's coverage. Read test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs and test/specs/ISS-0451.md directly. Check: every one of ISS-0451's 3 acceptance criteria has a runnable test covering it; no skipped/deferred coverage; fixtures are isolated (this test shares Pollers/PollersBreaker singletons with pollers_test.exs -- confirm no ordering/isolation hazard, e.g. via async: false and clean teardown). Then, per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md's mutation-testing section: TEST-DESIGNER reported applying 2 mutants (trip-threshold removal in pollers_breaker.ex; reverting application.ex's :temporary child-spec change) and recorded both failing the new test as expected. You must INDEPENDENTLY APPLY AT LEAST ONE of these two mutants yourself and re-run the test, per that workflow section's explicit rule ('accepting the reported pass counts is copying a claim, not validating one') -- do not simply trust TEST-DESIGNER's own report of the mutation results. Use the same revert-and-verify discipline (git checkout -- after, git status --porcelain empty, clean re-run confirmed) -- a mutant left in the tree is a step failure in itself.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict confirms all 3 of ISS-0451's ACs are covered by a runnable test, citing specific test functions
Verdict confirms fixture isolation (async: false, singleton-sharing hazard addressed)
At least 1 of TEST-DESIGNER's 2 reported mutants independently re-applied and re-run by this validator, with the result quoted
Confirmation the mutant was reverted and the tree verified clean (git status --porcelain empty) before this handoff completes
A FAIL verdict lists every gap; a PASS verdict states exactly what was independently re-derived
